Theory gives the bias, variance and coverage of an estimator
only for simple estimators and simple data distributions.
A simulation study estimates the same properties for any estimator a computer can run.
It generates many data sets from a distribution whose parameters are known,
applies the estimator to each,
and summarizes the results.

This page defines the parts of a simulation study,
shows how to measure the study's own accuracy,
and works one example in R and Python whose exact answer is known.
